properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency of the backend's Ethereum signing stack (eth-sig-util → ethereumjs-util → elliptic → hash.js@1.1.7), which ships SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512 in the backend build. No direct application call site; the algorithms are exercised inside the ECDSA recovery library on the live auth path. Changeable by upgrading the dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live security control: Math.random() generates the one-time login challenge nonce that users must sign with their Ethereum key — once at user creation (db.ts:19) and re-rolled after every successful login (controller.ts:77). Math.random is a seeded PRNG predictable from observed outputs, weakening the replay-protection property of the personal_sign challenge; should be crypto.randomInt()/randomBytes(). The most finding-grade first-party issue in this repo alongside the hardcoded JWT secret.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 ships in the frontend dependency tree as a transitive dep of selfsigned@^1.10.8 (react-scripts 4 dev-server tooling) — it generates the CRA HTTPS dev certificate (RSA keygen + X.509 self-signing). Available in the shipped library set; no call site in application source, react-scripts toolchain only. Changeable here by bumping react-scripts. LIB-fe0eb9a4 records the same lockfile entry from the library side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency of the web3@^1.6.1 account/signing stack; secp256k1 is the curve of the Ethereum personal_sign login scheme. The frontend's live use is web3.eth.personal.sign at Login.tsx:41 (reported as a separate finding); the library itself ships in the frontend bundle and is reachable through web3 whether or not app code names it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The backend's entire session-token scheme in one config: HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) minted at services/auth/controller.ts:86-95 via jwt.sign(config.secret, {algorithm: config.algorithms[0]}) and verified by express-jwt at services/users/routes.ts:15,22 with the same config object. The secret is the hardcoded literal 'shhhh' at config.ts:6 — 40 bits, in source, with a TODO to move it to env. Any party that can verify can mint (shared-symmetric design); secret also lives in the frontend-reachable repo. M

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the library that actually performs the personal_sign ECDSA recovery authenticating every login (call site at services/auth/controller.ts:48, reported separately). The dependency entry itself is the build-ships-it record: elliptic 6.5.4 has known security advisories worth noting on upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.1.0 is a transitive dependency of web3@1.6.1's Ethereum stack (ethereum-cryptography@^2.x → @ethereumjs/util); provides secp256r1/P-256 ECDSA+ECDH among others. Available in the shipped bundle; the app's own login chain uses MetaMask secp256k1, so P-256 is shipped-but-unused. Same lockfile entry as scout-1 object LIB-e9aa10c7 (@noble/curves).

properties.name: pqs:context

LIB-a0bfbc1a records the same lockfile entry from the library side.
